company: Ministerio de Ambiente, Vivienda y Desarrollo Territorial
card_says: Described in the present tense as 'the Colombian environment, housing and territorial development ministry', which ran the project through its vice-ministry for water and sanitation.
source_says: Verified. Decreto 3570 de 2011 recites that Law 1444 of 2011 'ordenó que se escindieran del Ministerio de Ambiente, Vivienda y Desarrollo Territorial, los objetivos y funciones' and 'reorganizó el Ministerio de Ambiente, Vivienda y Desarrollo Territorial ... y lo denominó Ministerio de Ambiente y Desarrollo Sostenible'. Its articles place the Viceministerio de Agua y Saneamiento Básico at the Ministerio de Vivienda, Ciudad y Territorio. The ministry held the water and sanitation vice-ministry at the time of the case; from 2011 it did not. The decree does not itself call the housing ministry new, so the card should not be corrected to say it was created in 2011.

source.title: Decreto 3570 de 2011
source.publisher: Ministerio de Ambiente y Desarrollo Sostenible, Colombia

company: Fondo Financiero de Proyectos de Desarrollo (FONADE)
card_says: Named as FONADE, 'the Colombian state development project financing agency', which administered the sub-projects.
source_says: Verified. It carried the FONADE name at the time of the case; article 1 of Decree 495 of 2019 provides that Fonade 'se denominará, en adelante, Empresa Nacional Promotora del Desarrollo Territorial (ENTerritorio)' and describes it as an 'Empresa Industrial y Comercial del Estado de carácter financiero ... vinculada al Departamento Nacional de Planeación y vigilada por la Superintendencia Financiera'.

company: Aguas de La Guajira S.A. E.S.P.
card_says: Named as the operator of the Riohacha water supply system, in a 2011 resettlement plan about events of 2001-2006.
source_says: Verified. The regulator records that the company was constituted 'con el nombre de AGUAS DE LA GUAJIRA S.A. E.S.P.', that 'el 13 de septiembre del 2014 se realizó la venta de las acciones mayoritarias de la empresa', and that it changed 'razón social a AVANZADAS SOLUCIONES DE ACUEDUCTO Y ALCANTARILLADO S.A. E.S.P.'. It operated under the card's name at the time of the events. The same document also classes it as 'una empresa privada constituida como sociedad anónima', and gives three different service start dates (1 December 2000 in Table 1, 1 May 2001 in 1.2.1, 'el año 2001' in section 1), which is left unreconciled.

company: Agence Djiboutienne d'Execution des Travaux d'Interet Public (ADETIP)
card_says: 'In 2007 Parliament widened its mandate to the National Initiative for Human Development and it was renamed Agence Djiboutienne de Developpement Social (ADDS), into which ADETIP was folded.'
source_says: Corrected, and the conflict is inside one document. The project's own completion report carries both readings: 'In November 2007, Parliament approved a law creating a new agency, ADDS (the Social Development Agency), with the broad mandate of implementing all poverty reduction programs ... As a consequence, ADETIP would be folded into the new agency', and, twelve pages later, 'in 2007, the Government decided to broaden the mandate of ADETIP, and make it the agency in charge of implementing the National Initiative for Human Development, (INDH). Its name was changed to ADDS.' The card merges the two. ADDS's own site dates its establishment to Decree No. 0025 of 8 January 2008 and describes it as resulting 'from the merger of the former Djibouti Agency for the Execution of Public Interest Works (ADETIP) and the former Social Development Fund (FSD) project'. A 2007 law and a 2008 founding decree are not inconsistent; the card's single sentence, which makes it both a renaming and a folding-in, is not supported by either source alone.

source.title: Djibouti - Flood Emergency Rehabilitation Project (Implementation Completion and Results Report), paras. on institutional changes; and About ADDS
source.publisher: World Bank; Agence Djiboutienne de Développement Social

company: Ministry of Information and Communication Infrastructure (MOICI), The Gambia
card_says: Named as the ministry made responsible by the resettlement plan for carrying it out, through the state telecommunications company.
source_says: Verified. The successor ministry's own infographic dates the name: the Department of State for Communications and Information Technology was set up in 2002, renamed Ministry of Communications, Information & Information Technology in 2009, renamed Ministry of Information and Communication Infrastructure in 2011, and in 2022 'MOICI was decoupled' into the Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy and the Ministry of Information. The ministry held the card's name at the time of the case.

card_says: Named as North Macedonia's national road agency and the implementing body for the road upgrade, with its Director as project coordinator.
source_says: Verified, and the name conflict is in the source itself. The successor's history page says amendments to the Law on Public Roads of 11 July 2008 created the 'Agency for Public Roads' as legal successor to the Fund for National and Regional Roads (1996-2008), and that a law of 27 December 2012 established the Public Enterprise for State Roads, which 'took over the rights, responsibilities, employees, property, assets and archives of the Agency for State Roads'. The page uses two different names for the body it describes and does not explain the change, which is left unreconciled. The country was the Republic of Macedonia throughout the agency's existence.

source.publisher: Public Enterprise for State Roads, North Macedonia

card_says: The entity is spelled 'Comité Permanent d'Acquisitions à l'Amiable' and called the Haitian government's land acquisition committee.
source_says: Verified. The Bank's Haitian resettlement framework gives the name in the singular, 'Comité Permanent d'Acquisition à l'Amiable (CPA)', and states 'le CPA, siégeant au MEF, s'occupe de l'identification et du paiement des expropriations pour l'État haïtien' - that is, at the Ministry of Economy and Finance and not at the public works ministry. The same section adds that the predecessor Comité d'Évaluation, operating since 1994, was based at the MTPTC, that 'depuis quelques années, le CE ne fonctionne plus', and that 'cette structure a évolué en un Comité Permanent d'Acquisition à l'Amiable (CPA)'.

source.title: Cadre de politique de réinstallation, Haiti Digital Acceleration Project (P171976)

company: Housing Fund of the Ministry of Urban Development, Djibouti
card_says: The fund is attached to a 'Ministry of Urban Development'.
source_says: Verified, with a date caveat the writer did not state. The 2018 report says 'public housing policy falls under the purview of the Delegate Ministry' (MDMHUEL), a delegate ministry within the Ministry of Habitat, Urban Planning and Environment, which 'was created in 2011', and that the ministry 'implements most of its key directives through two main bodies: the FH and the Djibouti Real Estate Company'. That arrangement post-dates the 2004-2009 case on the card, so it corrects the ministry's name as of 2018 and says nothing about which ministry the fund sat under when the 277 dwellings were built. The same report says 'the FH is being relaunched as the Agency for Urban Rehabilitation and Social Housing', a planned step as of 2018 and not a completed one.

source.title: Home improvement: the provision of housing remains a critical component of development plans (The Report: Djibouti 2018)

company: Unité de Coordination des Projets (UCoP), Ministry of Planning
card_says: The entity is named 'Unité de Coordination des Projets (UCoP)'.
source_says: Added by the checker. The project's own documents do not agree on the name. The 2007 financing agreement defines it in the singular: '"UCOP" means Unite de Coordination du Projet, established and operating pursuant to Decree 03/023 dated September 10, 2003'. The 2008 resettlement policy framework also uses 'Unité de Coordination du Projet' and dates it to presidential decree 'n° 03/024 daté du 10 septembre 2003'. The two decree numbers are left unreconciled. The 2013 completion report's abbreviation list gives 'Unité de Coordination de Projets' and its text elsewhere 'Unité Coordination des Projet'.

source.title: Financing Agreement for Grant H282-ZR (Conformed), Appendix para. 34; Cadre de politique de réinstallation, PURUS, section 6.3; Implementation Completion and Results Report

company: State Commission for Roads and Bridges, Ministry of Construction, Housing, Municipalities and Public Works, Iraq
card_says: The commission is placed in the 'Ministry of Construction, Housing, Municipalities and Public Works'.
source_says: Added by the checker. The 2014 loan agreement defines the body as sitting in a differently named ministry: '"State Commission for Roads and Bridges" and the acronym "SCRB" mean the commission within the Ministry of Construction and Housing, or any successor thereto', and the appraisal document places the project management team 'at SCRB within the Ministry of Construction and Housing in Baghdad'. The 2023 completion report records the later change: the government's restructuring 'involved the creation of the Ministry of Construction, Housing and Public Municipalities (MOCHPM) followed by a further change to subordinate RBD as a department under the MOCHPM with the responsibility for strategic planning and management of national roads network and expressways'. The ministry name on the card belongs to the later period, and in that later period the body named on the card is the Roads and Bridges Directorate.

source.title: Loan Agreement for Loan 8322-IQ (Closing Package), Appendix para. 23; Iraq - Transport Corridors Project (Implementation Completion and Results Report), para. 36
